v.why: Under Adam a wider net takes larger function-space steps, so at lr near the 0.278-1 cliff widening pushes training into divergence.
Lower gradient noise from a bigger batch stabilises large Adam steps that are otherwise erratic.
The L2 term is divided by batch size, so small batches get a stronger effective penalty and a larger alpha over-shrinks.
The L2 penalty sums over all weights, so wide nets feel a stronger total shrinkage and over-regularise sooner.
Extra layers amplify instability at large Adam steps, making divergence or dead ReLUs more likely.
Depth and width are parallel capacity routes, so an extra layer helps most when narrow width is the bottleneck.
Large batches leave few updates in 243 epochs and deeper nets need more updates to optimise.
Strong L2 compounds across additional layers and drives the net toward a constant predictor.
Narrow nets move slowly per step and underfit at small lr, so they gain more from larger steps.
With a single hidden layer width is the only capacity route, so shrinking it bottlenecks the net.
